outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: In his evening address on Wednesday, reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 8:10 p.m. EET Wednesday (12:10 p.m. CT), President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, following a briefing from Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal, that the electricity-supply situation was currently most severe in the Kharkiv and Sumy regions and also difficult in the Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava regions, and that there had been strikes on Odesa and its surrounding region, as well as on the Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia regions. He said repair crews were working in all the affected regions and must be provided with the necessary personnel and equipment, that Ukraine had secured the resources required to carry out these repairs, and that additional support packages were being prepared in coordination with partners. He did not give a national customer count or customer counts for those regions. That evening assessment is later than Ukraine's Energy Ministry Wednesday-morning statement. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:13 p.m. EET Wednesday (5:13 a.m. CT), said Russia had carried out more than 1,000 strikes on energy facilities since September, primarily targeting high-voltage substations, and that the attacks had caused new power outages in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Sumy, Rivne, and Cherkasy regions as of Wednesday morning. The ministry said the situation remained extremely difficult in the Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions, that energy workers were doing everything possible to restore supplies as quickly as possible, but that repeated attacks were significantly complicating repair work, and that Russia was deliberately targeting energy facilities, including those where repairs were almost complete. It said Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo reported that by Tuesday evening, it and NPC Ukrenergo had once again restored electricity to 390,700 consumers. The ministry said scheduled hourly power-outage schedules were in effect in most regions of Ukraine, that power-consumption restrictions applied to industrial consumers, and that emergency power cuts were being implemented in the Sumy, Kharkiv, and Poltava regions. It also said an energy worker was injured in an enemy strike in Kyiv region on Tuesday. The ministry did not give a national customer count or customer counts for those regions. That Energy Ministry statement is later than Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning statement, which had listed the same eight regions as having consumers without power due to attacks and had said emergency outages were currently being applied in the Kharkiv and Sumy regions; the ministry's later account also named Poltava among the regions under emergency cuts. No official national customer count was found. Later Wednesday evening, after that morning regional list was issued, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on energy facilities of another company in the south of Odesa region had caused outages. Suspilne, in a 6:16 p.m. EET Wednesday report (10:16 a.m. CT) citing DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi's Facebook page, said part of customers in the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts were left without electricity, that the attack caused significant destruction at those facilities, that specialists began inspecting equipment and clearing rubble once it was safe, and that restoring the damaged facilities would take time. Ukrinform, in a 7:04 p.m. EET Wednesday report (11:04 a.m. CT) citing a Telegram post by Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, said the strikes caused power-supply disruptions in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts, that no casualties had been reported, and that energy crews were assessing the damage and working to restore electricity. NV, in a 7:16 p.m. EET Wednesday report (11:16 a.m. CT) also citing Kiper, likewise said outages were being recorded in parts of those two districts, that there were no injured, and that energy workers were assessing the aftermath and working on restoration. No customer count was given for that Wednesday-evening southern Odesa outage. Ukrenergo, in a Wednesday morning statement reported by DSnews at 11:03 a.m. EET Wednesday and carried by malva.tv at 11:07 a.m. EET Wednesday, said enemy attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure were continuing and that, as of Wednesday morning, consumers were without power in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Sumy, Rivne, and Cherkasy regions. Ukrenergo said the most difficult situation, because of repeated Russian attacks, was in the Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk regions, and that emergency outages were currently being applied in the Kharkiv and Sumy regions because of damage to energy equipment. It said that in some regions, through the end of the day, capacity-restriction schedules would remain in effect for industry and hourly outage schedules of 1 to 3 groups would remain in effect for all categories of consumers, and that up-to-date schedules should be checked on each region's distribution-system operator. It did not give a national customer count or customer counts for those regions. Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne Regional Military Administration, said in a Telegram post reported by Ukrinform at 8:50 a.m. EET Wednesday and by Interfax-Ukraine at 9:02 a.m. EET Wednesday that a Wednesday morning Russian attack had left more than 80 settlements in the north of Rivne region without power; he said there was no information about wounded, and that energy workers had already started restoration work. No customer count was given for that Rivne outage. That Wednesday-morning regional list supersedes Tuesday afternoon's list of regions with attack-related outages and emergency cuts. On Tuesday evening, Ukrenergo, in an announcement reported by Korrespondent at 8:17 p.m. EET Tuesday and by UNIAN at 8:46 p.m. EET Tuesday, said that on Wednesday, Nov 18, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of Ukraine because of the aftermath of attacks on the energy system: capacity-restriction schedules for industry, and hourly outage schedules of 1 to 3 groups for all categories of consumers. UNN, citing Ukrenergo in an 8:07 p.m. EET Monday report, said one group equals four hours without electricity, so those scheduled outages may last from 4 to 12 hours. UNIAN also published Wednesday hourly schedules for the Kharkiv, Poltava, and Sumy regions: in Kharkiv region, it said outages would run from midnight to midnight and would last at least 7 hours for some groups and up to 12.5 hours for others; in Poltava region, 9 to 11 hours depending on the group; and in Sumy region, 8 to 16 hours depending on the subgroup. Those Wednesday schedules remain in effect, alongside Wednesday emergency cuts. Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning statement named emergency cuts in the Kharkiv and Sumy regions; the Energy Ministry's later Wednesday statement, reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:13 p.m. EET, also named Poltava among the regions under emergency cuts. No official national customer count was found. Earlier Tuesday, Ukrenergo, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 12:57 p.m. EET, said Russian attacks on Nov 17 left some consumers without power in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Rivne, Sumy, Chernihiv, and Chernivtsi regions, and that emergency power cuts were also being implemented in the Kirovohrad, Poltava, and Sumy regions because of significant damage to equipment. Ukrenergo said that in some regions, through the end of that day, power-consumption restrictions would remain in place for industrial consumers and scheduled hourly power cuts affecting one to three groups would remain in place for all categories of consumers. It did not give customer counts for those regions. Earlier Tuesday, Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 11:24 a.m. EET, had listed the same nine regions as having some consumers without power, said the situation was extremely difficult in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia, where Russia has been continuously attacking energy facilities in the Dnipro region since last week, and said air-raid alerts were delaying repairs and that restored facilities were being attacked again. At that hour, the ministry said emergency outages were being applied in the Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Poltava, and Kharkiv regions because of equipment damage and reduced voltage on the high-voltage network, and that hourly outage schedules were in effect in most regions of the country, with capacity-restriction schedules for industry. Before those morning attacks, Ukrenergo had already said planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock on Tuesday, Nov 17, in parts of Ukraine: capacity-restriction schedules for industry, and hourly outage schedules of 1 to 3 groups (queues) for all categories of consumers, because of the aftermath of attacks on the energy system. LB.ua, citing Ukrenergo, published that Tuesday schedule update at 10:18 p.m. EET Monday. DTEK said new Tuesday-morning strikes left 700,000 households without power in Dnipropetrovsk region (see the separate Dnipro row). In Zaporizhzhia and the region, Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo reported a mass outage around 8:00 a.m. EET Tuesday; as of 2:00 p.m. EET, the company said it had re-energized critical infrastructure and a significant portion of residents and legal entities, but had to suspend restoration work because of the threat of further attacks, and that work would continue until supply was fully restored. It gave no customer count for that Tuesday outage. Later Tuesday evening, the acting head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, Mykhailo Semikin, said in a Telegram post reported by Ukrinform at 8:31 p.m. EET Tuesday that emergency power outages in the region had been completely cancelled and that hourly outages continued. ZPRZ.city, in a 9:23 p.m. EET Tuesday report, said the Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo press service reported at 7:43 p.m. EET Tuesday that, on Ukrenergo's order, special emergency outage schedules and emergency outage schedules in Zaporizhzhia region had been cancelled in full, and that hourly outage schedules remained in effect. Inform.zp.ua, in a 7:00 a.m. EET Wednesday report citing Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo, published Wednesday hourly schedules for all six queues in the city and region. Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning statement again listed Zaporizhzhia among regions with consumers without power due to attacks, but it did not say emergency cuts had been reimposed there and did not give a customer count. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian strikes late Monday on the city's North and South bridges over the Dnipro, and on some other infrastructure, caused some water and power cuts, traffic restrictions, and partial damage to the subway; Reuters reported that account on Tuesday. No official customer count for the Kyiv power cuts was found. DTEK Kyiv Regional Power Grids said a Tuesday attack hit an energy facility in the Boryspil district of Kyiv region, damaging equipment, and that crews were waiting for permission from the State Emergency Service and the military before inspecting the site; Ukrainska Pravda published a 7:01 p.m. EET Tuesday account of that Boryspil-district strike, citing DTEK, and TrueUA had published an earlier account at 5:23 p.m. EET Tuesday, citing DTEK's official channel. DTEK Kyiv Regional Power Grids later said emergency outages that had been applied in parts of the Boryspil and Brovary districts on Ukrenergo's order were cancelled as of 2:25 p.m. EET Tuesday, and that stabilization outage schedules were again in effect in the region, according to kyivshchyna.info, which cited that 2:25 p.m. update and said the emergency cuts had lasted at least 30 minutes. No official customer count for those Kyiv-region emergency cuts was found. On Monday evening, Nov 16, Ukrenergo said enemy strikes had caused large-scale power outages in eastern Ukraine and that the situation was particularly difficult in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Poltava, and Zaporizhzhia. DTEK said the city of Dnipro was completely without power Monday evening after an attack on energy facilities in the region; as of 7:27 a.m. EET Tuesday, before the later Tuesday-morning strikes, Dnepr.info, citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi, said electricity had been restored for some residents, with emergency outages still in effect in parts of Dnipro and nearby districts (see the separate Dnipro row). DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 on its facilities in the north of Odesa region left 52,200 households without power (see the separate Northern Odesa region row). No later official restoration figure for that outage was found after a Wednesday-morning recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page. Overnight Nov 15, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack left 41,000 customers without power in the Odesa region, including Chornomorsk (see the separate Odesa region row). No later official restoration figure was found after that same recheck. Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning list of regions with consumers without power due to attacks did not include Odesa; that is not an official restoration figure for those earlier Odesa outages. In a Nov 17 statement, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said an energy facility in the south of the region was hit overnight Nov 17, that customers were re-energized where technically possible, and that 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power; it said repairs would take time and gave no restoration time. That 3,300-customer figure is for the overnight Nov 17 southern attack and is not a later official count for the earlier northern or Chornomorsk outages. The Mykolaiv Regional Military Administration said a Monday-evening Shahed-238-type drone attack left 76 settlements in the Pervomaiskyi district without electricity; Mezha, citing a regional administration briefing as of 7:30 a.m. EET Tuesday, said electricity had been restored to all 76 settlements. Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning list of regions with consumers without power due to attacks did not include Mykolaiv. Cherkasyoblenergo, in an 8:58 p.m. EET Nov 16 statement, said consumers in the Uman district were without power and that hourly outage schedules there temporarily did not apply; it gave no customer count, and no later official Uman restoration figure was found. Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning statement listed Cherkasy among regions with consumers without power due to attacks, without a customer count and without naming Uman. On the Nov 15 Zaporizhzhia attack, Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine, said electricity supply to 359,000 consumers was disrupted and was later restored that day; a Monday afternoon attack again substantially limited supply in the city, and the company said the situation had been stabilized by the end of Monday, with three-queue hourly schedules for the population, before Tuesday morning's mass outage. Sumyoblenergo, in a Nov 16 update reported by SUMYTODAY, said part of Sumy region was still without a stable electricity supply for a second day after an accident at a high-voltage facility (no customer count); Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning statement listed Sumy among regions with consumers without power due to attacks and among those under emergency cuts, without a new customer count. On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; no later Chernihiv customer figure or confirmed restoration was found. Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning list of regions with consumers without power due to attacks did not include Chernihiv; that is not an official restoration figure for the Nov 13 Chernihiv outage. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the Odesa region; that weekly total does not give a later official figure for the morning Nov 16 or overnight Nov 15 Odesa outages. The Wednesday-evening southern Odesa attack described above, which DTEK said hit facilities of another company, is also not an official restoration figure for those earlier DTEK outages. In Russian-occupied parts of the Donetsk region, news-donetsk.ru, in a 1:30 p.m. local Wednesday, Nov 18 report citing occupation government chairman Andrey Chertkov, said 125,000 residential subscribers remained without electricity and 228 boiler houses were de-energized after temporary outages were reintroduced Wednesday morning (see the separate occupied Donetsk region row).

outages.cause: New Russian attacks on energy infrastructure on the morning of Nov 17, after earlier Nov 16 attacks on energy facilities in the region
outages.affected: 700,000 households without power in Dnipropetrovsk region after new Russian strikes on the morning of Tuesday, Nov 17, according to DTEK. Suspilne, citing DTEK's Telegram page in an 11:18 a.m. EET Tuesday report, said that after new large-scale Russian strikes on the region's energy infrastructure that morning, significant damage to energy facilities left 700,000 homes without power. It said the outages affected residents of Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohradskyi, Kamianskyi, and Samarivskyi districts, that crews were first restoring power to critical infrastructure, and that work was continuing wherever the security situation allowed. Censor.NET, also citing DTEK in an 11:22 a.m. Tuesday report, said 700,000 families were left without power in the region and likewise named Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohrad, Kamianske, and Samarivka districts. No official restoration time was given. This is a later, separate wave of outages from Monday evening, Nov 16, when DTEK, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 6:59 p.m. EET and Ukrinform at 7:08 p.m. EET, said that after an attack on energy facilities in the region, the city of Dnipro was completely without power, and that some residents of the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, and Kamianskyi districts were also without electricity. Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov, in a Monday Telegram post reported by NV at 7:10 p.m. EET, said that after Russian attacks on the city, almost half of Dnipro was without electricity, and he called it the sixth blackout in two weeks. He also said two people were killed, eight were in hospital, and 10 apartment buildings were damaged. As of 7:27 a.m. EET Tuesday, before the later Tuesday-morning strikes, Dnepr.info, citing DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi, said electricity had been restored for some residents, but that scheduled stabilization outages had not yet been introduced in the hardest-hit areas, and that emergency outages remained in effect, by Ukrenergo order, in parts of the cities of Dnipro, Kamianske, and Samar, as well as in the Samarivskyi and Dniprovskyi districts, Pavlohrad and the Pavlohrad district, and Solone and Tsarychanka, while scheduled stabilization outages were in effect in the rest of the region. Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 10:14 a.m. EET Tuesday, said crews had repaired equipment overnight but that new Russian attacks again caused damage and widespread outages, so restoration work had to start again. Dniprovska Poradnytsia, in a 9:48 p.m. EET Tuesday report, said DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi had published Wednesday, Nov 18, hourly stabilization-outage schedules for Dnipropetrovsk region, covering all consumer groups; that publication is a Wednesday schedule and is not an official customer count or a confirmation that the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household outage had been fully restored. D1, in a noon EET Wednesday, Nov 18 report citing energy companies, said that as of Wednesday morning, emergency outages were not being applied in Dnipropetrovsk region, and that stabilization (scheduled hourly) outages were in effect throughout the day by Ukrenergo order. DTEK Dniprovski Elektromerezhi said Russian shelling had left the networks operating at the limit of their capabilities, and that additional load when many powerful appliances are switched on after restoration can cause accidents. Dnepr.info also published Wednesday hourly stabilization schedules for DTEK and CEC (TsEK) customers in Dnipro and said emergency outages had been cancelled. That Wednesday-morning update is not a new official customer count and is not a confirmation that the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household outage had been fully restored. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in the Wednesday statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:13 p.m. EET (5:13 a.m. CT), again listed Dnipropetrovsk among regions with new morning outages and said the situation remained extremely difficult there; it did not give a customer count for the region. Zelenskyy, in the evening address reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 8:10 p.m. EET Wednesday (12:10 p.m. CT), said the situation was also difficult in Dnipropetrovsk region; he did not give a customer count for the region. No later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found.

outages.cause: Russian attack on DTEK energy facilities
outages.affected: 52,200 households without power, according to a Nov 16 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 hit its energy facilities in the north of Odesa region, that 52,200 households were temporarily left without electricity, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment in order to begin repairs as soon as possible, and that all work is being carried out under safety rules, including during air-raid alerts. DTEK also said the company's production site was damaged in the attack (windows blown out and ceilings and doors damaged) and that employees were not injured. No restoration time was given. This is a separate, later attack in the north of the region from DTEK's Nov 14 statement that a morning attack on one of its facilities there left almost 50,000 customers without power, and from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. In a separate Nov 17 statement, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said an energy facility in the south of the region was hit overnight Nov 17, that customers were re-energized where technically possible, and that 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power; that figure is for the southern Nov 17 attack and is not a later official count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the region; that weekly total does not give a later official figure for this morning Nov 16 outage. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found after the morning Nov 16 statement. DTEK OEM's official news page was rechecked Wednesday afternoon; it now also lists a Wednesday-evening item saying that on the evening of Nov 18 the enemy attacked energy facilities of another company in the south of Odesa region and that outages were being recorded. Suspilne, Ukrinform, and NV reported that those outages were in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts and gave no customer count. That Wednesday-evening southern attack is a later, separate event and is not an official customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. The Nov 16 statement remained the latest official figure found for this northern outage. Ukrenergo's Wednesday-morning list of regions with consumers without power due to attacks did not include Odesa; that is not an official restoration figure for this outage. A later Wednesday DTEK OEM item said crews would carry out urgent equipment repairs from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Thursday, Nov 19, with planned outages in parts of Izmail district and in Kyivskyi and Prymorskyi districts of Odesa and the suburbs; that is a planned Thursday repair outage and is not an official customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage.

Suspilne, Ukrinform, and NV reported that those outages were in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts and gave no customer count. That Wednesday-evening southern attack is a later, separate event and is not an official customer count or restoration notice for this overnight Nov 15 outage. outages.affected: No official customer count. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in a Nov 18 statement, said that toward evening on Nov 18 the enemy attacked energy facilities of another company in the south of Odesa region, and that outages were being recorded in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts. It did not give a customer count or a firm restoration time. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, in a Telegram post reported by Ukrinform at 7:04 p.m. EET Wednesday (11:04 a.m. CT) and by Interfax-Ukraine at 7:16 p.m. EET Wednesday (11:16 a.m. CT), said the strikes caused power-supply disruptions in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts, that no casualties had been reported, and that energy crews were assessing the damage and working to restore electricity. Suspilne, in a 6:16 p.m. EET Wednesday report (10:16 a.m. CT) citing DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi's Facebook page, likewise said part of customers in those two districts were left without electricity and that restoring the damaged facilities would take time. NV, in a 7:16 p.m. EET Wednesday report (11:16 a.m. CT) also citing Kiper, said outages were being recorded in parts of those two districts, that there were no injured, and that energy workers were assessing the aftermath and working on restoration. This is a later, separate event from DTEK's overnight Nov 15 outage that left 41,000 customers without power, from the morning Nov 16 northern outage that left 52,200 households without power, and from the southern Nov 17 DTEK attack after which 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said the destruction was significant and that repairs would take time.

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Khartsyzk, Torez, Debaltseve, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Occupation authorities said energy infrastructure was attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, causing an emergency in the regional power system. On Nov 15, the Russia-appointed head of the Donetsk occupation government, Andrey Chertkov, said the grid was damaged by a "powerful enemy attack," while some Russian media called it an accident. Vedomosti reported that Ukrainian forces struck energy infrastructure in the region overnight Nov 15. Later Tuesday and again Wednesday morning, occupation authorities attributed renewed forced outages to a shortage of available capacity and high grid load
outages.affected: Occupation authorities have not given a single independently confirmed total, and the latest official figures they issued still come from occupation sources. News-donetsk.ru, in a 1:30 p.m. local Wednesday, Nov 18 report citing occupation government chairman Andrey Chertkov, said temporary outages were reintroduced Wednesday morning because of a shortage of available capacity and high load on the networks. It said partial outages affected Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Debaltseve, Yenakiieve, the Yasynuvata municipal district, Khartsyzk, Torez, the Shakhtarsk municipal district, and Horlivka, and that 125,000 residential subscribers remained without electricity and 228 boiler houses were de-energized. Chertkov said specialists were taking the necessary measures to restore supply, and that as the situation stabilized and technical possibility appeared, supply would be restored to consumers in stages. An earlier 12:15 p.m. local Wednesday news-donetsk.ru report said energy workers had gradually restored supply overnight to Nov 18 to consumers disconnected the day before, but that temporary restrictions were reintroduced Wednesday morning because of a shortage of available capacity and high load, a measure it said was needed to protect equipment from serious accidents. That earlier report listed Donetsk, Makiivka, Horlivka, Debaltseve, Yenakiieve, Khartsyzk, Torez, and the Yasynuvata and Shakhtarsk districts, and said interruptions in the Amvrosiivka and Telmanove districts were caused by a cessation of supply from neighboring regions; it did not include the 125,000-subscriber figure, which appeared in the later 1:30 p.m. report citing Chertkov. These Wednesday figures supersede the earlier Wednesday 8:09 a.m. local news-donetsk.ru report, citing occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin and Donetskenergo (a branch of JSC Yugo-Zapadnaya ESK), that because permissible network load had been exceeded, 163 transformer substations were partially de-energized in the Kalininsky, Proletarsky, and Voroshilovsky districts of Donetsk and that 31,090 subscribers remained without electricity. Earlier Tuesday, Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:31 p.m. local Nov 17 report citing the occupation energy ministry, said forced temporary outages were in effect because of a shortage of available capacity and high load on the power system, measures it said were needed to prevent equipment overload and possible accidents. As of 8:00 p.m., it said partial outages affected Donetsk, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Mariupol, Makiivka, Torez, Khartsyzk, and Dokuchaievsk, as well as the Yasynuvata, Shakhtarsk, Telmanove, Amvrosiivka, and Volodarske municipal districts. The ministry said that if conditions were favorable, grid load was expected to stabilize by the end of the day, after which supply would be restored to consumers in stages. It did not give a customer count in that evening update. Later Tuesday, dnrnews.ru, in a 10:32 p.m. local report, said electricity supply was being restored in settlements of the Starobeshevo municipal district where supply had previously been suspended. It cited a post from the Starobeshevo municipal administration (via a channel attributed to Aleksey Cherkashin). It did not give a customer count. Earlier Tuesday, news-donetsk.ru, in a 9:09 a.m. local Nov 17 report citing occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin and Donetskenergo, said that because permissible network load had been exceeded, 122 transformer substations were de-energized in the Kirovsky and Leninsky districts of Donetsk and that 23,200 subscribers remained without electricity, with restoration work under way. News-donetsk.ru, in an 8:14 a.m. local Tuesday report citing the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, said energy workers had carried out the necessary restoration work and that most previously de-energized consumers had already been reconnected. It said the regional power system remained under strain, that because of a shortage of available capacity and high grid load, forced temporary outages were possible in Donetsk, Horlivka, and Yasynuvata, and that local outages were also occurring in Makiivka, Yenakiieve, Novoazovsk, and Shakhtarsk municipal districts. It said the outages were emergency in nature, were not planned in advance, and were introduced based on the current state of the grids and the load; it did not give a new customer count. RIA Novosti's Prime, in a Tuesday report citing the same ministry Telegram statement, likewise said most previously de-energized consumers had been reconnected and that the system remained under strain, without a new customer count. Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:30 p.m. local Nov 16 report, citing the occupation administration of the head and government of the occupied Donetsk region and Donetskenergo director Oleg Pavlyak, said 428,000 subscribers remained without electricity. Of those, it said 284,000 were de-energized because of the emergency shutdown of a power unit, and 144,000 household consumers were under a temporary capacity-limitation schedule (GVO) of 95 MW. It said the unit was expected to start by midnight, after which specialists planned to begin restoring supply to consumers in Donetsk, Mariupol, and the Novoazovsk, Volnovakha, and Novotroitsk districts. Earlier Monday morning figures, which have been superseded by later updates, included 201,220 subscribers without electricity in all districts of Donetsk, according to occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin citing Donetskenergo, as reported by news-donetsk.ru at 10:55 a.m. local Nov 16, and more than 133,500 subscribers without electricity in Mariupol, with 941 transformer substations in the urban district still de-energized, according to the occupation administration of the Mariupol urban district as reported by MRPL.NEWS at 9:41 a.m. local Nov 16. Later Wednesday, dnrnews.ru, in a 6:16 p.m. local Nov 18 report (9:16 a.m. CT) citing Chertkov, gave no new customer count. Chertkov said the priority was to supply the necessary voltage to idle boiler houses and resume heat supply to homes and social facilities, that energy workers were reserving capacity, and that temporary outages of residential customers were partly related to that. He said emergency crews were working continuously and that energy workers planned to reconnect all customers in the near future; that is not an official firm restoration time and is not a later official customer count. The 125,000-subscriber and 228-boiler-house figures from the 1:30 p.m. local Wednesday report remained the latest official counts found. These figures come from occupation authorities and were not independently confirmed in the sources reviewed. Later Wednesday, RIA Novosti, in a 10:28 p.m. Moscow time Wednesday, Nov 18 report (1:28 p.m. CT) citing occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin, said electricity supply had been restored for more than 500 transformer substations in five districts of Donetsk. Citing Donetskenergo (a branch of JSC Yugo-Zapadnaya ESK), Kulemzin said that after connection work, 226 transformer substations had been re-energized in the Petrovsky, Kievsky, Kuibyshevsky, and Kirovsky districts, that 232 substations had been connected in the Kalininsky, Kievsky, and Kirovsky districts, and that 88 substations had been re-energized in the Petrovsky district of Donetsk. Those figures are substation restorations in Donetsk city, not a remaining customer count, and they do not replace the 125,000-subscriber and 228-boiler-house figures from the earlier 1:30 p.m. local Wednesday report, which remained the latest official remaining counts found. These figures come from occupation authorities and were not independently confirmed in the sources reviewed.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. Chertkov, as reported by news-donetsk.ru at 1:30 p.m. local Wednesday (4:30 a.m. CT), said specialists were taking the necessary measures and that as the situation stabilized and technical possibility appeared, supply would be restored to consumers in stages. Later Wednesday, as reported by dnrnews.ru at 6:16 p.m. local (9:16 a.m. CT), he said energy workers planned to reconnect all customers in the near future; that is not an official firm restoration time.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns and maintenance. UNE's Wednesday bulletin, published by Juventud Rebelde, said that unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance
outages.affected: UNE's Wednesday bulletin, published by Juventud Rebelde at 10:22 a.m. Cuba time Wednesday (9:22 a.m. CT) and also summarized by CiberCuba at 7:58 a.m. Cuba time Wednesday (6:58 a.m. CT), is the latest official national forecast found: if forecast conditions hold, 1,790 MW affected at the evening peak, with 1,040 MW available versus 2,800 MW of demand (a 1,760 MW deficit). At 6:00 a.m. Wednesday, the grid had 1,040 MW available versus 2,240 MW of demand, leaving 1,198 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,250 MW affected at midday. On Tuesday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Tuesday affectation was 1,735 MW at 7:00 p.m. Tuesday. Tuesday solar photovoltaic output was 3,170 MWh, with a maximum of 493 MW at midday. The Wednesday bulletin said unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance. CiberCuba's transcript of the official parte said thermal generation limitations were 423 MW; Juventud Rebelde's reprint of the same bulletin said those limitations were 493 MW. The Wednesday bulletin no longer listed unit 8 of CTE Mariel among units in breakdown, a unit that had been listed in UNE's Tuesday bulletin. Official UNE and Juventud Rebelde sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid. On Wednesday, CiberCuba, citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, said that at 3:15 a.m. Cuba time Wednesday the utility reported 73 distribution circuits affected by a generation deficit, with 164 MW affected in the province. That remained the latest official Havana provincial total found. CiberCuba's Nov 18 daily summary, still citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, later reported additional deficit outages and restorations on Havana circuits through at least 12:03 p.m. Cuba time Wednesday (11:03 a.m. CT), including later affectations on circuits such as A219, A223, and A960; those circuit reports are provincial and are not a later official national UNE peak figure or a later official Havana total. CiberCuba's Nov 18 daily summary, still citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, later reported additional deficit outages on Havana circuits through at least 5:40 p.m. Cuba time Wednesday (4:40 p.m. CT), including later affectations on circuits such as C13, A1075, and A318; those circuit reports are provincial and are not a later official national UNE peak figure or a later official Havana total. CiberCuba's SEN status page, in a Wednesday update, still showed the morning bulletin's 6:00 a.m. and evening-peak forecast figures and listed Tuesday's 1,735 MW maximum as the latest recorded daily close; it did not publish an official Wednesday evening-peak actual. No official Wednesday evening-peak actual from UNE was found. On Monday evening, CiberCuba, citing the Empresa Eléctrica de Las Tunas, said the province was disconnected from the National Electric System at 6:02 p.m. Monday because of a system emergency; it did not give a customer count or a reconnection time. CiberCuba's Nov 18 daily summary said the provincial electric company reported 129 damaged transformers and pending interruptions in several municipalities, including 167 pending interruptions in Las Tunas municipality and 163 in Puerto Padre; those figures were not accompanied by a customer count or a clear official reconnection notice for the Monday disconnection.

outages.place: Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Pageview, Homestead Park, Jan Hofmeyr, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. City Power later said the first explosion was caused by cable theft. A separate Crown Substation fault and a Florida Glen cable theft also interrupted supply. On Sunday, City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown was needed to complete critical Mayfair Substation repairs
outages.affected: No official customer count from City Power. Daily Maverick, in a Nov 18 article, and The Citizen, in a 5:40 a.m. SAST Wednesday, Nov 18 report, both said that while the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and some industrial areas in Crown Mines had had power restored, more than 20,000 residents of Mayfair, Crown Mines, Homestead, Vrededorp, Pageview, Jan Hofmeyr, and Amalgam would have to wait for at least another week before their power came back on. That more-than-20,000-residents figure was reported by those newspapers and was not attributed to a City Power official count. The Citizen said the 49 residents of the Jan Hofmeyer Old Age Home in Vrededorp had been without power for nine days since the Mayfair substation fire. Daily Maverick, reporting from the home, likewise said residents there had been without power for nine days and that a water outage was also affecting the area, with Johannesburg Water listing the Brixton tower as empty. Both reports quoted City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena as saying that full power was restored after midnight on Sunday, that technicians were working on cable faults and on repairs at the Sentech tower, which he said had experienced multiple cable faults, and that engineers were attending to further cable faults affecting customers in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Homestead Park, Pageview, and Jan Hofmeyr. Mangena said Monday's work would focus on resolving the remaining faults, monitoring the network, and assessing its capacity to safely accommodate additional load, and that once the necessary repairs were completed and the network was sufficiently stable, the remaining customers would be restored in phases. He said City Power hoped to have this completed by the end of the week. The Citizen also said City Power started Monday morning with more than 3,100 open calls across the city, a citywide figure, not a customer count for the Mayfair-area outage. Those Mangena comments and the Monday open-call figure describe Monday's work and were published in The Citizen's Wednesday morning report and in Daily Maverick's Nov 18 article; no later official City Power restoration notice for the remaining Mayfair-area suburbs or for Sentech was found after those reports in a Wednesday-afternoon recheck. Earlier, SABC News, in a 10:01 a.m. SAST Monday, Nov 16 report, quoted Mangena saying that restoration shortly after midnight had brought several critical customers and sections of the network back online, including the SABC and Netcare Garden City Hospital, and that restoration work was continuing. He said parts of Crown remained outstanding and were scheduled to receive attention on Monday, and that technicians were also attending to further cable faults affecting customers in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Homestead Park, and Pageview, among others. eNCA, in a noon SAST Monday report attributing the update to City Power, said electricity had been restored to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and approximately half of Crown's industrial area, that residents and businesses in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, and Pageview remained without electricity because of ongoing cable faults, and that power to Sentech remained switched off for further maintenance and safety checks. A Wednesday-evening recheck found no later official City Power restoration notice for the remaining Mayfair-area suburbs or for Sentech.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given for remaining Mayfair-area customers or for Sentech. City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena, as quoted by The Citizen at 5:40 a.m. SAST Wednesday, Nov 18 (9:40 p.m. CT Tuesday) and by Daily Maverick in its Nov 18 article, said remaining customers would be restored in phases once repairs were completed and the network was sufficiently stable, and that City Power hoped to have this completed by the end of the week.

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. It said the strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, causing power outages that disrupted health services including dialysis and surgical procedures, access to clean water, and food production. AFP, in a Nov 17 report on the same OHCHR findings, likewise said the intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supplies had become a worrying trend, and quoted the report as saying that between Oct 20 and Nov 4 some 29 drone strikes attributed to the RSF hit electricity facilities and fuel stations, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. That official humanitarian account is later than an Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature, which said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. Al Jazeera said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found.
outages.updated: Nov 17, 2026 (UN in Sudan / OHCHR report, published Nov 17); AFP via Channels Television, Nov 17; Al Jazeera feature, published Nov 15; generation figure attributed to The Associated Press; rechecked 5:50 PM CT Wednesday, no official national customer count or restoration timetable found
